text:
anya: Heads-up — saw a weird regression on prod-4 yesterday where a single long-chat workload triggered cascading OOMs in the prefix cache layer. Putting notes here so we can decide mitigation options.

maria: ugh. is this the same tenant that was hitting large prompt windows last week?

anya: yes, same. They went from 8k->32k context in a canary and our shard sizing wasn't happy. KV cache hit-rate dropped and evictions spiked.

jonathan: quick numbers from the perf run I pulled: 
```
alloc_peak: 29.1GB
workspace_used: 4.2GB
kvcache_mem: 18.7GB
kv_hits: 0.62
evictions/sec: 210
ooms: 3 (worker restart)
kernel: cuda_attn_v2 (fallback to generic during pressure)
```

lee: interesting that kernel fallback is in the trace. That suggests our kernel selection heuristic flipped under memory pressure and workspace demand increased.

anya: exact sequence I think: long prefix -> KV shards swell (hot shard concentration) -> allocations fragment slab pool -> kernel selection avoids specialized fast kernels because free workspace under slab thresholds is too small -> token latency + memory churn -> eviction storm -> oom.

maria: can we be surgical: a) bias eviction toward cold shards early, b) apply a soft per-shard cap with spillover to disk/remote, c) prefer smaller-kernel paths if workspace cap is violated? Which is lowest risk to roll out?

jonathan: order of risk: c) is risky for latency but contained; a) is low risk; b) depends on infra (we don't have spill-to-disk infra for live Dedicated customers yet).

perf-bot: perf-sim results attached: sim run id=sim-2026-03-17-88, test profile: 10k seq, bimodal prefix locality. TTL=2h baseline. Outcome: soft-cap 0.8x reduces peak mem by 14% with hit-rate drop 4pp.

lee: can we try an emergency-handling path that doesn't require infra work: "emergency eviction bias + kernel-prefer". If a worker detects slab fragmentation above threshold X and kvmem > Y, it 1) set shard eviction bias to recency-weighted, 2) clamp new allocations for specialized kernels to a workspace_safety floor, 3) enable async background compaction of slab freelist.

anya: I sketched a POC patch this morning. It adds two switches: `runtime.prefcache.emergency_mode` and `allocator.compact_async_on_pressure`. The emergency_mode toggles `eviction_bias=hotdemote` -> `recency_demote` and reduces `kernel_workspace_limit_pct` from 30%->18% for that worker.

jonathan: can you paste the POC config snippet?

anya: sure:
```
# emergency POC
runtime:
  precache:
    emergency_mode: true
    shard_soft_cap_pct: 80   # allow spillover within worker, prefer demotion
    eviction_policy: recency_weighted
allocator:
  workspace_limit_pct: 18
  compact_async_on_pressure: true
  pressure_threshold_mb: 1024
```

maria: any microbenchmarks? how does that 18% workspace cap affect kernel selection latency?

jonathan: local microbench against the long-chat profile: median token latency +6ms, p95 +18ms, but peak mem down 12%. Kernel selection logs show fewer fallback-to-generic events (we force-check before fallback) because we avoid trying the big specialized kernel when workspace below threshold.

lee: +6ms median is acceptable if it prevents OOMs. What about hit-rate tradeoff on prefix cache? perf-bot sim said -4pp. Is that consistent with live traces?

perf-bot: live trace sampling (30m window) for that tenant: baseline kv_hit=0.69 -> emergency_mode kv_hit=0.66. Evictions drop after 10s. Overall token throughput for the tenant recovered 18% (less worker restarts).

anya: notable behavior: a few *cold* shards ended up being demoted aggressively and later re-primed causing transient extra allocation churn. We might want to add a small TTL extension for demoted shards (e.g., add 30s grace before fully evicting) to avoid churn loop.

maria: propose short rollout plan: 1) enable emergency_mode as feature flag for canary pool only 2) monitor kv_hit, evictions/sec, alloc_peak, kernel-fallback-rate 3) if metrics stable after 1h, widen to half of capacity.

jonathan: add instrumentation: `allocator.fragmentation_pct`, `kernel_fallback_count`, `shard_demotions/sec` to console dashboards. Also add an alert: kernel_fallback_count spike > 5/min => rollback.

lee: one more mitigation idea: dynamic TTL decay for hot shards. If a shard is repeatedly accessed > X/sec, temporarily increase its TTL to preserve hotness even under soft-cap. That will keep hit-rate up without growing global mem as much.

anya: agree — I'll add `ttl_bump_on_hot` with config: window=60s, access_threshold=25, bump_secs=120. Might reduce the demote-thaw cycle.

maria: ok patch + config changes look good. Who will own canary?

jonathan: I'll roll the canary in eu-prod-canary pool at 09:30 UTC and watch for the alerts.

anya: putting a PR up now: #3421 — includes POC runtime toggles, allocator compaction hook, and perf instrumentation.

maria: sweet. :thumbsup: keep notes here if you see anything surprising during canary.

perf-bot: alert subscription set for thread: kernel_fallback_count, evictions/sec, alloc_peak_gb.

lee: thanks all. follow-ups: anya add TTL-bump sim results to PR, jonathan deploy and add dashboard widgets, maria coordinate customer comms if canary triggers.

anya: noted. will link sim and a short runbook in the PR description.
